title: Imperative And Indicative Planning
definition: Imperative planning is a centralized, command-economy system where resources, production targets, and prices are rigidly controlled by the state, whereas indicative planning operates in a mixed economy where the state uses policy incentives, forecasts, and guidelines to steer private sector behavior without direct coercion.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial microtopic for UPSC Civil Services Examination under GS Paper 3 (Indian Economy and planning, resource mobilization, growth, development), tracing India's structural shift from socialist-leaning Soviet-style imperative elements in early Five-Year Plans to market-friendly indicative planning post-1991 LPG reforms.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Imperative And Indicative Planning.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic Economic Systems (Capitalism, Socialism, Mixed Economy)
History of Five-Year Plans in India
